feature: PowerShell "hello world" — proves the tenant connection itself (Connect-MgGraph + correct TenantId) works, independent of any specific write-action verification
notes: Part of Epic #803, third hello-world sibling of #957 (SQL) and #958 (UI) — same purpose:
prove a specific piece of the automation pipeline genuinely works before trusting anything
built on top of it. #900/#901 ASSUME the delegated PowerShell-to-tenant connection already
works; this manifest is the thing that proves that assumption is safe.
Single powerShellVerify step, deliberately with no apiTests/graphTests before it. `afterStep`
names "GRAPH_TEST_TENANT_ID" directly (no {{...}} needed — PowerShellTestExecutor wraps a
bare name in {{}} before calling TestRunVariables.Resolve), which resolves through #953/#961's
config-variable layer — checked BEFORE per-run extracted values — so this is the real
GRAPH_TEST_TENANT_ID Shane has set in Settings > Test Environment, not a value any step in
THIS manifest captured.
Ground truth cmdlet is (Get-MgContext).TenantId — Get-MgContext over Get-MgOrganization
because it's the cheapest possible real signal (local SDK context, no Graph round-trip) and
still gives a concrete GUID to diff, per #964's own "Get-MgContext (or Get-MgOrganization if
that gives a more concrete real value)" — TenantId on the context IS that concrete value.
compareField.matchType 'exact', case-insensitive GUID compare (PowerShellTestExecutor.Matches).
This single step covers both of #964's asks without any special-casing:
1. Connection succeeds via Shane's cached delegated identity — PowerShellTestExecutor's own
BuildScript always runs `Connect-MgGraph -UseDeviceCode -NoWelcome` before the cmdlet and
hard-checks $ctx.AuthType -eq 'Delegated'; if no valid cached token exists it detects the
device-code prompt on the child process's output and aborts within timeoutMs, failing this
step with the 'run Connect-MgGraph interactively once' message — never hangs. Nothing in
this manifest needs to re-implement that; it's already the executor's own behavior for
every powerShellVerify step, verified by reading PowerShellTestExecutor.cs directly.
2. Correct tenant, not just 'connected to something' — the exact-match diff against the real
GRAPH_TEST_TENANT_ID catches a stale cached session from a different engagement: if
(Get-MgContext).TenantId doesn't equal the configured testbed tenant, this step FAILS even
though the connection itself succeeded.
Shane To-Do precondition (documented, not verifiable from this headless environment): run
`Connect-MgGraph` interactively once in a pwsh 7 window signed in as himself (per #900), and
set the real GRAPH_TEST_TENANT_ID value in Settings > Test Environment Variables (per #953/
#961) — the #961 auto-discovery scan will pick up this manifest's GRAPH_TEST_TENANT_ID
reference and flag it needsReview with an <unset> default if it isn't already set.

powerShellVerify.name: tenant connection ground truth — Connect-MgGraph delegated identity resolves to the configured GRAPH_TEST_TENANT_ID
